knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots; entries 1..2 and a reconfiguration committed with full delivery, then node 5 moved to Prepare under a ballot with n 2 and given an AcceptSync whose log_sync carries the StopSign with sync_idx 2, an empty suffix and decided_idx 3.

knowledge.assertion: Control for the covering witness: sync_idx 2 with the same StopSign-carrying payload leaves accepted 3, decided 3, is_reconfigured Some and the marker at index 2, so the inflation is specific to a prefix that already covers the marker.
The contrasting covering case: sync_idx 3 raises accepted to 4, moves the marker to index 3 and clears its decided status.
The source arithmetic that distinguishes the two cases: the extra one is added for the StopSign on top of whatever the prefix already covers.
The randomized run shows the same distinction at scale: accepted reached 38 before any marker was present, and the marker later filled the last counted slot.

interpretations.rationale: The matched pair isolates the trigger for the accepted-index inflation. Receipt 8e598dd57d974a2e9d7a38157e6a1b4e ran acceptsync_before_stopsign_keeps_accepted (exit 0, test passed); its declared comparison is complete and holds. Event 0 records node 5 at accepted 3, decided 3 and is_reconfigured Some, with the StopSign at index 2 and nothing at index 3, and event 1 records exactly the same state after an AcceptSync carrying the StopSign with sync_idx 2. The earlier receipt 125641a1a75c4c9d93fd7667b11fb1b8 used the same follower, the same payload and the same decided_idx, changing only sync_idx to 3, and recorded accepted 4, decided 3, is_reconfigured None, index 2 absent and index 3 a StopSign, with its comparison violated. Because the only difference is whether the sync prefix already covers the marker's position, the extra increment is attributable to sync_log adding one for a StopSign on top of a prefix that already includes it, not to the StopSign's presence in the sync. In the randomized run the same condition appears at scale: nodes 1, 2 and 5 reached accepted 38 with no marker, the marker then appeared at index 37 without raising the index, index 36 stayed empty, and node 4 later decided 38 from those reported accepted indices while its own log ended at 37. Node 3, holding the marker at 36 with decided equal to accepted 37, received the Decides as its next expected sequence messages, clamped its decided index, sent no PrepareReq and was offered no AcceptStopSign because it already accepted one, so it stayed behind for the whole convergence window. The defect is therefore established with a controlled pair at the sync boundary and a seeded end-to-end witness of the resulting safety and progress consequences.
counterevidence: A follower that genuinely missed the AcceptStopSign can still recover: in the constructed clean-miss run the periodic Decide was sequence-ahead, the follower reconnected, and an AcceptSync repaired it.
A leadership change, or an external reconnected() call, leads to Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync, which gives the follower a fresh sequence and a log sync from the new leader.
The control shows the inflation is not caused by a StopSign-carrying sync as such: with a prefix that stops before the marker the same payload leaves the state unchanged.
The earlier zero divergence count is not counterevidence of agreement; it is an artifact of a comparison that ignores StopSign entries, holes and prefix lengths.
limitations: Both minimal cases deliver a crafted AcceptSync to a node placed in Prepare under a chosen ballot; they model the state transition rather than reproducing the network history that produced such a sync.
The randomized run samples transitions after each action and round, so a change and its reversal between samples would be missed; none is evident.
Five nodes, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots and no next configuration started; flexible quorums, batching and snapshot-based sync are unexercised.
